newsitem.title: USA: Lilly to advertise Prozac directly to consumers.
newsitem.headline: Lilly to advertise Prozac directly to consumers.

text.p: Drug manufacturing giant Eli Lilly and Co. said Monday it will begin consumer advertising for Prozac, its top-selling antidepressant that faces mounting competitive pressures.
The Indianapolis-based firm said the campaign will be launched in August in national consumer magazines, including Newsweek and U.S. News & World Report.
"Additional advertising is being planned but a specific schedule has not yet been determined," Lilly said.
The campaign will mark Lilly's second step into direct-to-consumer advertising. The company has previously advertised diabetes medication.

"This campaign is designed to give people with untreated depression hope and inspire them to seek the help they need," said Dr. Gary Tollefson, a psychiatrist and vice president of Lilly Research Laboratories.
Since its debut 10 years ago, Prozac has become the world's top-selling antidepressant and the third-largest selling U.S. drug of any type. Sales in 1996 were $1.69 billion.
To date, the medication has been prescribed for more than 17 million Americans, Lilly said.

More broadly, Prozac has entered the pop culture lexicon and become a touchstone for changing American attitudes about psychiatry. "In many ways, the introduction of Prozac helped change the way we view and treat depression," Tollefson said.

Prozac's market dominance is being challenged by rivals, such as Zoloft from Pfizer Inc., Paxil from SmithKline Beecham Plc, Effexor from American Home Products Corp. and Serzone from Bristol-Myers Squibb.
Through the fourth quarter of 1996 and the first quarter of 1997, Prozac held a roughly 20 percent market share among antidepressants, but its growth has slowed, analysts said.
The advertising campaign will be handled by the Chicago-based Leo Burnett USA advertising firm.
